clue.text: New Year's Eve, say, when horologists gather?

definitions.text: New Year's Eve, say, when horologists gather?

parts.words: New Year's Eve, say, when horologists gather?
parts.note: horologists are clock and timepiece experts, so a gathering of them is jokingly an evening of their favourite instrument; the real term is a church service seeing in the New Year

explanation.surface: Clockmakers hold a party on the last night of December.
explanation.walkthrough: A watch night is a late service held by some Protestant churches on New Year's Eve (and sometimes Christmas Eve); the clue pretends it is the night the timepiece enthusiasts meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the late church service held to see the year out is the best-known vigil of this name, so New Year's Eve is one instance.

clue.text: Passed time, we hear, with offers to trap river avifauna

indicators.note: signals that the words for passing time are to be taken by their sound, not their spelling

parts.note: whiled (away the hours) means passed time

indicators.note: the word for offers closes round the river letter, catching it inside

parts.note: bids are offers, as at an auction

explanation.surface: Someone idles about with bribes meant to catch the birds along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to trap' puts R inside BIDS to make BIRDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: avifauna is the bird life of a region, and untamed birds living freely make up that population.

clue.text: Sample country, moving South

indicators.note: the letter for South shifts to a new position within the word for country

parts.note: a state is a country
S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: A survey takes a sample of a nation whose population is drifting southwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' shifts the S of STATE from the front to the middle: S-TATE becomes TA-S-TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to sample food or drink is to try a little of it with the tongue.

clue.text: I am satisfactory, turning up in gardens in casual wear

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits inside the word for gardens

parts.note: hoes is a verb meaning gardens, works the soil with a hoe

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: 'I do' means I am satisfactory, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: Someone content with themselves pops up in the garden dressed casually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses I DO to ODI, which goes 'in' HOES. 'Gardens' is a verb here, not the noun it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: hooded sweatshirts are standard informal clothing, so they count as casual wear.

clue.text: Position of power's good in family

indicators.note: the letter for good is placed within the word for family

parts.note: kinship is family relationship

explanation.surface: Holding a powerful post is nice when it stays within the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the office or rank of a monarch is the supreme position of power in a realm.

clue.text: Fashionable place to host each and every mixed-media work?

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

indicators.note: the word for place receives the other piece inside it, as a host takes in a guest

parts.note: a station is a place or post, as in 'know your station'
all means each and every

explanation.surface: A trendy venue puts on a show of all sorts of mixed-media art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to host' has the place word take in the each-and-every word near its front. 'place' means a post or rank here, not a venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-plain art term: an installation is a gallery artwork assembled in a space, often combining several media.

clue.text: Work unit, including a European, picked up item of ammunition

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards
the work unit contains the European inside it

parts.note: an erg is a unit of work or energy in physics
a Dane, someone from Denmark, is a European

explanation.surface: A labour team, with a European among them, collects a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' gives E-DANE-RG, and 'picked up' reverses it. 'picked up' looks like collecting the item, but it is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hand-thrown bomb is one kind of munition, so it counts as an item of ammunition.

clue.text: Hard work restraining one over and over amidst evil rising masses

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: the word for work holds the letter for one inside it

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
I is the Roman numeral one
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top
the second over letter goes into the middle of the word for evil

parts.note: ill means evil, as in 'ill deeds'
O again, the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Hard labour, repeated endlessly, keeps the common people down amid growing wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over and over' gives two separate O's: one stands alone, and 'amidst' puts the other into ILL, making IOLL, which 'rising' turns upwards to LLOI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a Greek phrase for 'the many', used for the common people or the masses.

clue.text: Flourishing year following award

indicators.note: the letter for year comes after the word for award

parts.note: a palm is an award or prize, as in the Palme d'Or

explanation.surface: A business has a thriving year after winning a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: palmy days are prosperous, thriving times.

clue.text: Not so busy studying?

parts.note: less means not so much
on means happening or occupied, as in having a lot on

explanation.surface: Someone with time to spare wonders if they should be studying.
explanation.walkthrough: Having 'less on' means not being so busy; the question mark flags that the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose link: a class or session of tuition is a period of studying, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Particular observation about business district

indicators.note: the word for observation goes round the business district letters

parts.note: espial is the act of spying or observing
EC is the postcode of the City of London, its financial district

explanation.surface: Someone passes a specific remark about the financial quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postcode area covering the City, London's financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dated form of 'special', meaning exceptional or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: What has appeal, regularly, for artist at work?

definitions.text: What has appeal, regularly, for artist at work?

indicators.note: the letters are set working, rearranged into a new order
every other letter of the word appeal is taken

explanation.surface: Asks what keeps an artist's interest regularly while busy painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks PEL from appeal; 'at work' rearranges PEL with FORARTIST. The whole clue also describes the answer: a painter painting the face that most appeals to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a painting of the painter by the painter, the subject an artist has to hand whenever working.

clue.text: Second letter I have written about Hungary's area of industry

parts.note: bee is the spelt name of the alphabet's second letter
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A letter-writer reports on a Hungarian industrial zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts H inside IVE: I-H-VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a hub of busy work is likened to a bees' home, so a hive is a centre of industry.

clue.text: Thirteen characters absorbed in no matter which medical discipline

indicators.note: the thirteen letters are soaked up inside the word for no matter which

parts.note: any means no matter which
A to M are the first thirteen letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Thirteen students are absorbed in whichever branch of medicine they study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thirteen characters' is A TO M, the alphabet's first half, which goes inside ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the study of the body's structure is one of the founding branches of medical science.

clue.text: Primarily usable for sleep, possibly?

indicators.note: signals the letters may be arranged in another way
only the opening letter of usable is taken

explanation.surface: Describes something mainly good for a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' gives U from usable; 'possibly' rearranges U with FORSLEEP. Read whole, the clue describes something restful.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a restful, calm place or time is what you would choose for a nap.

clue.text: Objection over additional material artist excluded? It's readily perused

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a plaint is a complaint or objection

indicators.note: the artist letters are left out of the word for additional material

parts.note: extra means additional material
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: An editor objects to a padded text with the illustrator cut out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluded' removes RA from EXTRA, leaving EXT.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: unencrypted, ordinary writing is something anyone can understand at a glance.

clue.text: European monarch dismissing foremost mathematician

indicators.note: the opening letter of the monarch word is sent away

parts.note: a ruler is a monarch

explanation.surface: A European king sacks his leading scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing foremost' drops the R of RULER, leaving ULER. Leonhard Euler was an 18th-century Swiss mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Swiss-born pioneer of analysis and graph theory is among the greatest of all number scholars.

clue.text: Artist having little time to add to rock-band trademark

indicators.note: the letter for time is attached to the end of the other pieces

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band
a brand is a trademark
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A painter is short of time to design a logo for a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Dutch Golden Age master of light and shadow is one of the most famous painters.

clue.text: Suspends bones

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means postpones or halts, as a court ... proceedings
the stiffening strips, once whalebone, in a corset

explanation.walkthrough: Both meanings are archaic or legal enough to mislead: a court can halt an order, and old corsets were stiffened with whalebone strips.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to halt something legally, and the stiffening ribs sewn into a corset.

clue.text: NASA Sun shot having name of Mozart opera character

indicators.note: signals the letters are broken up and reassembled, as something shot to pieces

explanation.surface: A space agency photograph of the Sun is named after an operatic heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a photograph, but it rearranges NASASUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Figaro's bride, the clever maid in The Marriage of Figaro, is a leading role in that opera.

clue.text: Refusal to involve East German? Discrimination

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east
racism is discrimination on grounds of race

explanation.surface: Asks whether excluding someone from the former GDR amounts to prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like a person from the old GDR; it is the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: shunning or excluding someone from a group is a refusal to involve them.

clue.text: Classic victim of hunt, an age after the event

indicators.note: the piece for an age comes after the piece for the event

parts.note: an act is an event or deed
A is the indefinite article, same as an
an eon is an age

explanation.surface: A hunting casualty is remembered a very long time afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Actaeon saw Artemis bathing; she turned him into a stag and his own hounds killed him.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the hunter of Greek myth changed into a stag and torn apart by his hounds is a classical victim.

clue.text: Is upset by SF film, having a fixed view

parts.note: minds means objects to, is upset by
E.T. is Spielberg's science-fiction film

explanation.surface: A viewer is annoyed by a sci-fi movie because of rigid opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal, but 'Is upset by' is simply MINDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an established attitude or way of thinking that is hard to shift is an entrenched outlook.

clue.text: Run from blue deer

indicators.note: the run letter is taken away from the word for blue

parts.note: morose means gloomy, blue
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A deer flees from the sad one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes R out of MOROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the largest species of the deer family, called elk in Britain.

clue.text: Happen to interrupt medic, losing day? Month

indicators.note: the word for happen breaks into the shortened medic word
the day letter drops out of the medic word

parts.note: a doctor is a medic
be means happen or take place, as in 'let it be'

explanation.surface: Someone chances to interrupt a doctor who has lost a day in the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' leaves OCTOR, the medic with its day letter gone; 'to interrupt' breaks it before the final R. 'Happen' is the plain verb BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the tenth month of the calendar year is one of the twelve.

clue.text: Fetch book round

parts.note: a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go and get the book on the table nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fetch something is to carry it here.

clue.text: Once at sea with a Scotsman, covering Pacific 26

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Once afloat, a Scot travels across the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges ONCE plus A to OCEAN. 26 refers to the answer at 26-across, REGION.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective: Oceania is the region of Pacific islands, so the term describes what belongs to or spans that area.

clue.text: Say I will invade centre of incorrect area

indicators.note: the say and I letters push their way into the shortened word for incorrect
only the middle of the word for incorrect is kept, its outer letters removed

parts.note: wrong means incorrect
eg (for example) is a way to say 'say'

explanation.surface: An army declares it will invade the heart of an improper zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' keeps RON, the middle of the incorrect word with its ends trimmed; 'will invade' pushes EGI into it after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a district or tract of land is an area.

clue.text: Area in middle of scenery depicted in theatre music

indicators.note: the area word is placed inside the central letters of scenery
the central three letters of the word scenery are taken

parts.note: a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: A space in the middle of the stage set is shown with incidental music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the central three letters of the seven-letter scenery. The answer is French for 'between act'.
explanation.definitionFit: French term: music played in the interval between acts of a play or opera.

clue.text: See 1
